name: David's Reign
summary: Follow David from the news of Saul's death through his rise to the throne of a united Israel, his worst sin, and the family rebellion that drove him from his own capital and back again.

stops.locationNote: One of over a dozen proposed sites (Khirbet er-Ra'i shown here); no candidate has a confirmed destruction layer matching this period.
The Ammonite capital, at the site of the citadel in modern Amman. David joined the siege in person to finish it (2 Samuel 12:29).

On the Jerusalem-to-Jericho road near the Mount of Olives; several sites have been proposed (Ras et-Tumein, Barruka, Abu Dis) and sources disagree on which is likeliest, so this marker is only an approximate position in the right general area.
East of the Jordan near the Jabbok River; the exact site is disputed, with Tulul edh-Dhahab among the proposals.

East of the Jordan near the Jabbok River; the exact site is disputed, with Tulul edh-Dhahab among the proposals. David stayed at the city gate rather than joining the battle in the forest of Ephraim (2 Samuel 18:2-4).
The river crossing near Jericho where David's supporters met him on his return, not a single fixed site.
Saul's former capital, identified with Tell el-Ful.

David was holed up at Adullam, not Bethlehem itself, when three of his men broke through Philistine lines to bring him water from Bethlehem's well (2 Samuel 23:13-17). The city mound's identification with Adullam is still inconclusive, and the specific cave shown to visitors today is a separate, later tradition rather than an excavated find.
Traditionally identified with the Temple Mount, the same site marked for "the land of Moriah" in the Genesis patriarchs journey.
